title: Fool Operation
text: Trash watched that exchange with an unpleasant look on his face, I say. He’d been scheming to sow discord among the heroes, and yet here we were, united. So, how about that? What did he think of this scheme of mine?
“Boo!”
Suddenly, one of the Three Heroes Church pigs came charging out from a corridor with a dagger, as these things tend to happen.
“Shooting Star Shield!”
“Boo-hee!?”
“Not invited, I’m afraid.”

Faster than a flash, before the pig could even reach Father’s Shooting Star Shield, Itsuki, still riding atop Rabbit Guy, had already shot it through. The pig went flying spectacularly and got pinned to the wall.
“Boo-boo-boo—”
Before it could say anything else, Itsuki finished it off with an arrow straight between the eyes, quick as you please. Did he get it? Oh? Yep, dead as a doornail.
“Whoa……”
Ren looked thoroughly unsettled. Knowing Itsuki, I’d have expected him to just knock it out, but no mercy there at all.
“I sensed murderous intent, so I went ahead and killed it.”
“Ugh, come on…… seriously, you’re getting to be as fast as Motoyasu-kun now…… could you maybe hold back a little? The Queen’s right here, you know?”
“I’d say attempting to murder a hero you dislike right in front of the Queen is a full-blown game-over move all on its own, don’t you think?”

How about that? Itsuki turned to the Queen with a beaming smile. Father sometimes wore a smile cold enough to freeze hell over, and Itsuki’s expression right now belonged to that same family. The Queen hid her mouth behind her fan and pressed a hand to her forehead as if in lament, shadowing her eyes.
“Yes…… indeed. We shall not pursue the matter of how such a person is dealt with. Truly lamentable.”
Apparently this one had been some representative-class figure from a certain noble house, incidentally.
“Ha! This kind of sneak attack seems right up your daughter’s alley too—the eldest one, I mean.”
At Itsuki’s words, Trash’s brow furrowed.
“Are you saying you’d kill Malty the same way, should she appear!? I won’t allow it!”

“If that’s how you feel, then you’d best shield her before I ever get the chance to act. Fufu…… though honestly, I have my doubts your daughter’s even a follower of this Three Heroes Church business.”
“That child is devout.”
“That child hasn’t a shred of faith in her.”
The Queen answered as if flatly denying every word Trash had said.
“To that child, the Three Heroes Church is nothing more than a tool to be used. She only harassed Iwatani-sama because it was convenient for her.”
“I can guess as much just from how she flatters that king over there, and from the state of the country.”
“Nano.”
Rival looked over at me. I could answer that I already knew the reason, if asked.

“Fufu, I’d wager the root cause stirring up these Waves is that very princess, wouldn’t you? She’s hiding something. Something even her own parents have been fooled by. Before you go blaming Naofumi-san for everything, perhaps you ought to hand out a proper punishment for your daughter’s outrages? I look forward to it.”
Itsuki’s shots kept landing dead center.
“On that matter, what is to be done has already been decided.”
“W-what did you say!? What are you planning to make Malty do!?”

“Aultcray? You bear some responsibility in this yourself. If you wish to salvage anything, you have no choice but to distinguish yourself appropriately in this incident…… though I doubt you’ll be a match for the heroes in terms of combat prowess, so accordingly……”

The Queen was subtly threatening Trash. A punishment for the Crimson Swine, perhaps? I wanted to dish out even more punishment to that creature myself. Come to think of it, the day was fast approaching when I’d finally deliver its comeuppance and personal hell.

Making Father and the others suffer was one thing, but I still had to make it pay, and pay dearly, for poisoning Fleon-chan. The loop where I’d reunited with Fleon-chan had been the last loop in which I’d actually managed to punish that creature. The next loop had already had it disposed of from the start. Truly, something to look forward to.

Even giving it the same treatment as Takt wouldn’t be nearly enough to satisfy me. I had to keep devising ever more brutal methods of processing the Crimson Swine. Well…… either way, the first order of business would probably be shipping it off to Pig King, the very fate the Crimson Swine had raised such a fuss about in that very first world, wouldn’t it? Of course, first I’d let it swim free a while, watching for the chance to make it drink its own poison. Knowing the Queen, she’d likely settle things for now with expulsion from the royal family and stripping of power. She was probably scheming to smooth over relations between Trash and us. Executing the Crimson Swine outright would be too hasty a call. So she’d hand down a lenient judgment while dangling the threat of shipment to Pig King over its head. Well, at the moment, every single backer the Crimson Swine might have leaned on for support had already been crushed, making pardon nearly impossible—surrounded on all sides. Takt, its last fallback option, I’d already turned into an eternal art piece on Seven Cleft Island. Either way, I’d let it swim a while yet, all the better to make it suffer.

Fufufu…… indeed. It’d be quite the spectacle, seeing what kind of performance Trash put on. As I mused on such things while we advanced, a faintly similar situation flickered across my mind. Had I done something like this before?
“Rival.”
Most reluctantly, I called out to Rival in a low voice.
“Nano, what is it?”
“I get the feeling I’ve seen this mood inside the castle somewhere before, but perhaps it’s just my imagination?”
“Ah, Spear Hero. You’ve got a hunch too, nano? The circumstances differ, but there’s no mistaking the similar atmosphere, nano.”
“Similar to what? Tell me, I say. I chose the unknown path, did I not?”

“Well, you know, a fake king occupying the castle while you march in with the Queen to reclaim it—it overlaps with a loop Gaelion remembers, nano. Well…… though this one’s on a smaller scale, there sure are more people milling about here, nano.”

While chatting about this and that, we arrived at the throne room, I say. Waiting there were…… a faintly familiar, extremely well-built, muscle-bound sort of priest, and Trash’s body double, apparently? And also a reddish-black pig. That reddish-black pig also rang a faint bell. Given that the Three Heroes Church supposedly occupied the place, I’d assumed the Pope would be lying in wait here this time, but no sign of him? If anything, this was the new pope who’d shown up in the loop where we’d headed to Faubrey. I see, so Rival was right—the atmosphere really did resemble that decisive battle in the castle from the loop where we’d gone to Faubrey. Less ominous than back then, though. The unpleasant mood down in the castle town was plenty present, but the degree of ruin was different. Public order had declined, but nowhere near as badly ravaged as that time.
“So you’ve come this far, have you—you fake heroes, and the traitorous vixen impersonating the Queen, and the foolish king who’s let it all go to his head!”
Trash’s body double and the burly priest glared daggers at Ren.

“How dare you betray our trust and waltz in here, dragging along that fake king’s procession and the Demon King of the Shield besides! And now it turns out this generation’s Sword Hero is a fake too, one of the Demon King’s cronies! For trampling upon our faith, I shall pass judgment upon you all!”
Trash’s body double spat these words at us. In my memory his skin had looked purplish, but no, quite an ordinary complexion here. A fake Trash, I say.
“You thought you could move about without me noticing, but it was all completely see-through! Don’t think you can fool me! Which one’s the real king is plain as day…… the Demon King’s cronies……”

“Ren, you’ve got to act properly. Even if this Sword Hero, Shadow Saint, attempts an Illusion Induct to deceive me, before my Evil True Eye that sees through all falsehood, it’s nothing but a hollow Fool Operation. Which one is the real king, the Ultimate Sage, is something I, master of darkness, can always tell!”
Ren stared at his father and furrowed his brow.
“There’s no way we’d be doing that kind of performance here! Cut it out already, Naofumi!”
“But if we don’t, people might start thinking you’re the fake, right, Ren? You know, like…… something like that?”
There was a strong suspicion that Rafumi had spoken in that exact tone whenever dealing with this particular breed of opponent.
“Guh…… shut up, shut up! Itsuki! Movie skip!”

“Now, now, it wouldn’t do to skip past such an important scene of yours, Ren-san. I think I’ll just do a bit of filming here myself. Can’t let Kuro-san miss out on seeing your heroic figure, after all.”
Before I knew it, Itsuki had already pulled out a recording crystal and was setting up to film.
